name: Idaho

agency.name: Idaho Department of Lands, Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (OGCC) / Oil and Gas Program

form.name: Application for Permit to Drill, Deepen, or Plug Back
form.number: OGR-101 (revised June 2025), 4 pages; fee schedule OGR-100
form.notes: Read all 4 pages of the blank fillable form (HTTP 200, 238 KB): page 1 fees, denial reasons, completion and log rules; page 2 operator and well description; page 3 purchased-lease, surface owner, state leases, actions checkboxes, maps; page 4 other required information, certification, office-use box (Approval Date, US Well Number, Operator Number). Fee: drill $2,000, deepen $500, plug back $500 (printed on the form). Filed by mail to Boise. Rule: IDAPA 20.07.02.200; Idaho Code 47-316.

api_number.n: US Well Number (USWN 11-075-20041) on each well file page; also an office-use box on the form

permit_number.n: No separate permit number seen; the USWN identifies the permit and well

well_name.n: Well file page title ('James #1-10'); form asks Name of Lease and Well Number

operator_name.n: 'Operator:' on each well file page; form has Name of Operator

operator_id.n: 'Operator Number (if known)' in the office-use box

operator_type.n: Not on the OGR-101 checklist; not verified elsewhere

bond.n: 'Bond Type and Number' (if lease purchased with wells); denial for failure to post required bonds

county.n: 'County:' on well file page and on the form

district.n: Not on the OGR-101 checklist; not verified elsewhere

surface_latlon.n: Latitude, Longitude (decimal degrees) and datum on the form

surface_plss.n: Section, Township, Range and footages from section lines

bottom_hole_loc.n: Plat must show surface and bottom-hole locations for directional wells

lateral_path.n: Directional or Horizontal Drilling box; attachment required under IDAPA 20.07.02

surface_owner.n: 'Surface Rights Owner (at proposed surface location)'; state-lease boxes (a person's name not copied)

well_type.n: 'Type of Test/Unit': Gas / 640 acre or Oil / 40 acre or Other

proposed_depth_md.n: 'Proposed Measured Depth' on the well file page; form has 'Proposed depth'

proposed_depth_tvd.n: 'Proposed Total Vertical Depth' on the well file page

lateral_length.n: Not on the OGR-101 checklist; not verified elsewhere

target_formation.n: 'Estimated depth to the top of the target formations'

formation_tops.n: 'Estimated depth to the top of the important geologic markers'

casing_program.n: 'Proposed casing program': size, weight, setting depth

cement_program.n: 'Type and amount of cement to be used, and the intervals cemented'

pressure_control.n: 'Schematic diagram of the BOP and well head assemblies' with size and pressure rating

h2s.n: Not on the OGR-101 checklist; not verified elsewhere

pit_waste.n: 'Pit Construction' box (attachment); erosion control and reclamation plans

water.n: Not on the OGR-101 checklist; not verified elsewhere

fracture_plan.n: 'Well Treatment' box; a separate well-treatment application is posted for comment

frac_dates.n: Rule and Well Treatment form ask for no job date; the report is due within 30 days after the job

frac_chemicals.n: Application lists compound names and CAS (rule 211); report must show a FracFocus filing; no posted disclosure seen

frac_additives.n: Form OGR-004 asks trade name, supplier, purpose and SDS per additive; the one posted treatment lists none

frac_amounts.n: Form asks percent by volume and total volume of each additive and proppant, before and after the job

spacing_unit.n: Type of Test/Unit (640 or 40 acre, or Docket No.) and acres in lease(s)

spacing_exception.n: 'Is Operator requesting a well location exception?' Yes/No

mineral_owner.n: Not on the OGR-101 checklist; not verified elsewhere

fee.n: Drill $2,000, Deepen $500, Plug Back $500 printed on the form

notice_hearing.n: Page posts applications for 10 business days of public comment (lists seismic and well treatment)

date_received.n: 'Date:' beside the operator block and the signature date; not published as data

date_approved.n: Permit to Drill file name starts with the date (2026.02.04_...); 2 of 8 since 2019 are amended files dated later

date_expires.n: Not on the OGR-101 checklist; not verified elsewhere

spud_date.n: Not on the OGR-101 checklist; not verified elsewhere

completion_date.n: Not on the OGR-101 checklist; not verified elsewhere

status.n: 'Well Status:' (e.g. Drilled/Confidential) on each well file page

plat_image.n: Survey plat required; the posted Permit to Drill PDF is a combined file (not opened)

form_image.n: 'Permit to Drill' PDF linked from each well file page

completion_report.n: Form says a completion report is due in 30 days; not seen online for a well

logs.n: LASFiles.zip: LAS logs for wells drilled 2007 and later that are releasable

production_link.n: Page: monthly production exports to .csv from the Data Explorer; PDF reports per month

sources.name: OGCC Well & Facilities Files (index of every well on file and one HTML page per well, with its signed Permit to Drill)
sources.license: State web pages; some documents marked confidential by submitters are posted only where public
columns: Document Links (Permit to Drill, Sundry Notice 1..n)
USWN and well name in the index
activity_types: well permit to drill, sundry notices; wells in Bonneville, Canyon and Payette counties
sources.tested: Read 2026-11-01 with a plain automated agent, 3 s apart: the index (148 KB) lists 34 wells (3 Bonneville, 2 Canyon, 29 Payette) plus 2 gas facilities, 2007 to now, and links one WordPress page per well (about 140 KB each, 200 throughout). A page has 'Well Status:', 'County:', 'Operator:', depths and document links; the 'Permit to Drill' link is the signed permit PDF, whose file name starts with a date (2026.02.04_... or 20211002_...). The page's meta tags also carry the day WordPress made it (0 to 13 days after an approval). The producer reads the file-name date and never opens the PDFs. The file-name date is not always the approval date: for 2 of the 8 permits since 2019 the posted file is the permit as amended and its first page is the amendment's approval letter (3 and 1 months after the first approval, read from the signed letters). 35 requests, about 4.9 MB, 2 minutes 35 seconds.

sources.tested: The app answers without a login: a JSON search (api/Search/?t=Well&search=<API>) and the well detail pages (ED.aspx), read 2026-11-01. The detail's 'Date Issued' agrees with the signed permit for the two revised permits and for most others but is not reliable as an approval date: for one well it holds the application's intake day (9/13/2021 for a permit approved 10/2/2021) and the newest well (approved 5/22/2026) still shows 'Application Received' with its intake day. Not used. The CSV export was not tested (it exports production). Page last updated Nov 28, 2025 (OGCC page footer).

sources.name: OGCC 'Report to the Commission' (quarterly PDFs, 2020 Q1 to 2026 Q2) with a monthly 'Well & Permit Activity' table
sources.tested: 24 reports downloaded once, 3 s apart. 'APDs Approved' by month (2020 Q1 to 2025 Q2): 2020 Oct 1; 2021 Jun 1, Oct 1, Nov 1; 2022 Sep 2; 2023, 2024 and the first half of 2025 none; these match the well pages month by month from 2021 to mid-2025. The one difference is Oct 2020: a permit the Commission's own comment says was 'approved by OGCC October 26, waiting on Contested Case'; its signed permit is dated June 16, 2021. From Q3 2025 the table counts applications received, not approvals. 2019 has no quarterly report on the site.

grade_reason: Idaho issues about one permit to drill a year (8 since 2019). Every well it has permitted has a free page with its status, county, operator, proposed depths and the signed Permit to Drill, whose file name starts with the date. Held to B, not A: there is no bulk file or API with the date, it comes from the file names of 34 pages (two amended permits needed their first approval read from the signed letters), and the Data Explorer's 'Date Issued' is not reliable. Updated 2026-11-01: a producer reads the pages each week (35 requests) and its permits match the Commission's own quarterly 'APDs Approved' counts month by month from 2021 to mid-2025; the Data Explorer does answer without a login (a JSON search and a public map layer), but neither holds a trustworthy approval date.
producer_plan: Built: d11_nat_id.py. Reads the well index and each well's page (35 requests, 3 s apart, about 2.5 minutes, plain automated agent, no refusal) and counts one permit per well by the date at the start of its 'Permit to Drill' file name, from 2019 (only the new band; every other band and the fluid are null: the Commission posts no dated list of amendments, well treatments or injection permits). ORIGINAL_APPROVAL holds the two dates of permits whose posted file is the amended permit, keyed by the amended file's date and held to the page's creation date. A permit file that says revised or amended, or whose date is more than 5 days after or 60 days before its page was made, and is not in that table, fails the run with the date to look up: a new amended permit turns the weekly run red until a person reads it. Operator and county come from the page's own lines ('Snake River O&G' is mapped to the company's full name before the naming rule). The last 30 days are not shown. Fewer permits than the committed file refuses the run.
privacy_notes: Well pages show the operator company; permit PDFs and the form carry contact names, telephone numbers, e-mail addresses and surface-owner names, which are never opened or copied. The OGCC page names a staff contact and a public commenter (not copied).
